Your phone won't play bitchute vids because bandwidth allowance is not the same as concurrent connection allowance.

If you stream a video from a single provider, the pipe opened is very efficient. That ~1Gig of HD video will cost the network 1.5 Gigs. But if you use a client that is crowdsourced, like a torrent client, it opens x # of connections to conduct the assembly of the video file from numerous sources. The connections to addressing systems and agents is also very bandwidth consuming, not in terms of raw bandwidth but in 'cpu' intensive numerous connections.

So the bottom line is, all things are not equal and a metric of bandwidth is meaningless without more information about limitations on their network hardware and artificial limitations built into basic settings in your Android environment which were designed by Telcos.
